name: 粤语 (Cantonese; Hong Kong written and spoken)
summary: Cantonese is a separate Chinese language, not a Mandarin dialect. This file targets Hong Kong Cantonese in written-Cantonese Traditional characters with Jyutping (tone numbers 1 to 6). Round 2 verified Jyutping on all entries against words.hk 粵典 (the Hong Kong dictionary that gives Jyutping and examples) and Wiktionary, fixed 七仔 (cat1 zai2, not chat1 jai2), and added sentence-final particles with functions (啦, 喇, 喎, 囉, 嘛, 㗎, 嘅, 啩, 咋, 咩), spoken vocabulary (嘢, 咁, 點解, 邊個, 乜嘢, 唔該 vs 多謝, 攰, 癐), and sentence patterns (A-not-A, 咗/過/緊, 畀, comparison, passive). Cantonese is the best-sourced file of the four. Examples marked constructed:false come straight from dictionary example sentences.

grammar.standard: 他 / 她 / 它; 他们
grammar.condition: Third person pronoun, no gender. 佢哋 = plural. CUHK example: 我同佢拍緊拖.
grammar.romanization: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 paak3 gan2 to1

grammar.condition: Joins a possessor or a modifying phrase to a noun. words.hk example: 係我嘅 'it is mine'; 佢係呢度最靚嘅女仔 'the prettiest girl here'.
General negative before a verb or adjective, e.g. CUHK: 我唔係好熟佢. 唔 is a syllabic nasal 'm'.
grammar.romanization: ngo5 m4 hai6 hou2 suk6 keoi5

grammar.standard: 没有 (not have) / 还没 (not yet)
grammar.condition: 冇 = 'do not have / did not' (negates 有 and past events, no 唔). words.hk: 佢冇食晚飯, 我冇事. 未 'not yet' (also a sentence-final question: 你去過德國未？).
Verb suffix for completed action; also after an adjective for a changed state. words.hk: 食咗飯未呀？/ 你瘦咗又靚咗喎！
grammar.romanization: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3

grammar.condition: Experience marker; the situation no longer holds, in contrast to 咗. English Wikipedia: 我喺香港住過一年 (no longer living there).
grammar.romanization: ngo5 hai2 hoeng1 gong2 zyu6 gwo3 jat1 nin4

grammar.condition: Progressive marker after the verb. words.hk: 我食緊飯, 你而家做緊咩呀？
grammar.romanization: nei5 ji4 gaa1 zou6 gan2 me1 aa3

grammar.condition: Place preposition and 'to be at'. words.hk: 我屋企喺灣仔.
grammar.romanization: ngo5 uk1 kei2 hai2 waan1 zai2

grammar.condition: Preposition 'with / and'. CUHK: 我同佢拍緊拖.
Spoken form of 來. words.hk gives lai4/lei4, e.g. 你幾點嚟啊？ Written 來 versus 嚟 is disputed in Wikipedia's Written Cantonese article; use 嚟 for spoken lines.

grammar.standard: 一些 / 较 (a bit more; plural)
grammar.condition: Plural/some before a noun, and 'a bit more' after an adjective. words.hk: 好啲喇 'better now', 呢隻薯片好味啲 'this one tastes better'.
Yes/no questions repeat the verb with 唔. CUHK-type example from English Wikipedia: 你識唔識講廣東話？ Two-syllable verbs repeat only the first syllable: 鍾唔鍾意.
grammar.romanization: nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2

grammar.condition: Tag or question with 係唔係; words.hk: 佢係唔係做錯咗？— 係㗎。
grammar.romanization: keoi5 hai6 m4 hai6 zou6 co3 zo2

grammar.condition: Prohibition. words.hk: 咪郁！舉高雙手！ (mai5 juk1! 'Don't move!'). Note 咪 mai6 'then' is a different word.
Ditransitive order: the thing comes before the person. English Wikipedia: 畀嗰本書我.
Comparison after the adjective: 佢高過我. Without a standard: 佢高啲.
Passive needs an agent; if unknown use 人. English Wikipedia: 筷子畀人用咗.
grammar.romanization: faai3 zi2 bei2 jan4 jung6 zo2

grammar.standard: 疑问词 (question words keep the statement word order)
grammar.dialect: 邊個 / 乜嘢 (咩) / 邊度 / 幾時 / 點解 / 點樣
grammar.condition: Question words stay in the same place as the answer. Examples: 你係邊個？ / 你去咗邊度啊？ / 你而家做緊咩呀？ / 點解嘅？
grammar.romanization: nei5 heoi3 zo2 bin1 dou6 aa3

grammar.condition: 咁 'so, that (much)' before an adjective. Wiktionary example: 做咩你咁冇腦㗎？ Do not confuse with gam2 噉 'in that way'.
grammar.romanization: zou6 me1 nei5 gam3 mou5 nou5 gaa3

vocabulary.note: Everyday 'thing, stuff'. Derogatory when used for people: 衰嘢 / 死嘢 are insults ('rotter'). Euphemism for sex or ghosts in certain phrases: avoid in innocent lines (搞嘢).
'so, that much'. Not 噉 gam2.
Why. Also 做咩 / 做乜 / 為乜.
How. Also: 你呢排點樣呀？ 'how have you been recently?'
Who / which one.
What. 咩 is the short form; as a sentence-final particle me1 means surprised doubt.
Where; 'anywhere' in negative sentences; ironic 'how could'.

vocabulary.standard: 谢谢 / 麻烦你 / 不好意思
vocabulary.note: Used for 'thanks' for small favours or services, 'excuse me' to get attention, and 'please' when requesting. Said with irritation it means 'shut up / get lost'. For gifts or large kindness use 多謝.
Thanks for gifts and big favours; 唔該 is for services and small help.
Sorry. Also 'let someone down'.
Tired. Both characters read gui6. words.hk: 你個樣好攰喎。
Angry, upset. words.hk: 你仲未嬲完我呀？
Good-looking, also good in quality or feeling.
Luckily; also 'lucky'.
Look for; contact; earn.
Sleep or lie down.
Home; also family. Not 家 gaa1.
No need to.
Free, not busy. 你聽日得唔得閒呀？
Settle, finish, handle.
Correct; fits; coincidentally (咁啱). Shows the ng- drop in some speakers.
Waste. 好嘥囉 'such a waste'.
Two senses: 'serves you right' (harsh, teasing) and 'witty, hilarious'. Tone decides.
Like. 你鍾唔鍾意佢呀？
Afraid, worry. 佢好驚老婆㗎。
Adverb 'then, so' often with 囉: 你鍾意咪攞去囉。Different from 咪 mai5 'don't'.
Date, go out together.
Middle-aged married woman. Mildly derogatory, so do not use it as a direct address.
Hong Kong nickname of the convenience store. Round 1 had 'chat1 jai2', which was wrong; words.hk gives cat1 zai2.
English loan for bus; measure word 架 or 部.
Wiktionary: Hong Kong 的士, colloquial 老的; Taiwan 計程車. Jyutping of 的士 not checked on a Cantonese dictionary.
Do not know. words.hk 呀 aa3 example: 唔知啊 (m4 zi1 aa3).

particles.function: Basic sentence-final softener. Ends a general question (咩事啊？), an answer with a personal stance (唔知啊), lists (咖啡呀，奶茶呀) or, drawn out, conveys irritation.
particles.example: 而家幾點啊？ (ji4 gaa1 gei2 dim2 aa3)

particles.function: Confirmation or echo question: turns a statement into a question; with 都 'cannot be helped'.
particles.example: 你食緊飯呀？ (nei5 sik6 gan2 faan6 aa4)

particles.function: 'Oh, so...?': voices a just-realized fact for confirmation; also 'surely not...?' with negatives.
particles.example: 你唔會冇帶到銀包咓？ (nei5 m4 wui5 mou5 daai3 dou3 ngan4 baau1 aa5)

particles.particle: 呀嘛 aa6 maa5 / 嘛 maa5
particles.function: Corrects the hearer with a doubting tone ('shouldn't it be... ?', 'are you kidding?'). words.hk example: 冇嘢嘛 mou5 je5 maa5 'are you really OK?!'
particles.example: 唔係呀嘛？你講真㗎？ (m4 hai6 aa6 maa5? nei5 gong2 zan1 gaa4?)

particles.function: Requests, suggestions, and decisions made now (好啦！我自己做啦！); lists; 'of course' (梗係賣晒啦！); hesitant agreement when drawn out (好啦⋯⋯); ironic taunt (你開心啦？).
particles.example: 唔好等喇，走啦！ (m4 hou2 dang2 laa3, zau2 laa1)

particles.function: Marks a new situation or change of state: 'now it is...' (夠鐘喇, 好喇, 我好飽喇). The exact function range was not stated in the sources, only shown in examples.
particles.example: 唔使幫我喇。 (m4 sai2 bong1 ngo5 laa3)

particles.function: Sentence-final particle appearing in CUHK examples: 佢就會嘞; 就噉嘅，... 已經打好咗嘞. Nuance not explained there.
particles.example: 佢就會嘞 (keoi5 zau6 wui5 laak3)

particles.function: 'I've just noticed / by the way / you know': a newly noticed fact, or a reminder of something the hearer forgot.
particles.example: 佢遲到喎！ (keoi5 ci4 dou3 wo3)

particles.function: Quotes someone else's words with no responsibility, or ironically stresses the opposite ('...apparently').
particles.example: 媽咪話唔好飲汽水喎！ (maa1 mi4 waa6 m4 hou2 jam2 hei3 seoi2 wo5)

particles.function: Surprise or disapproval at something unexpected.
particles.example: 佢扮唔識我啝！ (keoi5 baan6 m4 sik1 ngo5 wo4)

particles.function: Points out something obvious ('of course', often with 咪); explains the reason; closes a list ('and so on'); strong opinion; resignation ('no choice then').
particles.example: 係囉！ (hai6 lo1)  /  上頭叫到，唯有做囉。(soeng6 tau4 giu3 dou3, wai4 jau5 zou6 lo1)

particles.function: Judgement on a change (好囉, 弊囉); decision ('走囉'); gentle suggestion ('落街行下囉？').
particles.example: 走囉，再唔走就冇車喇。 (zau2 lo3, zoi3 m4 zau2 zau6 mou5 ce1 laa3)

particles.function: Firm statement of fact or suggestion: 'let's...'.
particles.example: 不如食M記囉。 (bat1 jyu4 sik6 Mem1 gei3 lo4)

particles.function: Emphasis or insistence (contraction of 嘅 + 呀 according to round 1 source); also gaa4 = challenge-question, gaa2 = doubt or reservation.
particles.example: 呢啲係好嘢嚟㗎！ (ni1 di1 hai6 hou2 je5 lai4 gaa3)

particles.function: Sentence-final particle with several functions: 'why?' (點解嘅？), exclamation, hedging ('seems so'), downplaying ('no big deal').
particles.example: 點解嘅？ (dim2 gaai2 ge2)

particles.function: Speaker is not sure ('I guess').
particles.example: 我返屋企食麵啩。 (ngo5 faan1 uk1 kei2 sik6 min6 gwaa3)

particles.function: 'Only, just'; zaa4 asks 'only that?'.
particles.example: 仲有三個咋。 (zung6 jau5 saam1 go3 zaa3)

particles.function: Question particle showing doubt or surprise; also pronoun 'what'.
particles.example: 你當我傻嘅咩？ (nei5 dong3 ngo5 so4 ge3 me1)

particles.function: Surprise 'huh?' or a repeating question; also verb suffix 'for a bit' (著吓).
particles.example: 你食咗啦吓？ (nei5 sik6 zo2 laa3 haa5)

particles.function: Asserts something or expresses strong appreciation/praise (Wiktionary). No sentence examples were given.
Downplays: 'just, only a little'. Seen in a words.hk example 擦損咗少少啫 'just scratched a bit'. Function inferred from that example.
particles.example: 擦損咗少少啫，冇咩嘅。 (caat3 syun2 zo2 siu2 siu2 ze1, mou5 me1 ge2)

pronunciation.rule: 'Lazy sounds' (懶音) among younger Hong Kong speakers: n- → l- (你 nei → lei), ng- → zero (我 ngo → o), gw- → g-, kw- → k-. English Wikipedia calls them non-standard but increasingly common.
pronunciation.actor_tip: For a young, casual Hong Kong character use lei5 for 你 and o for 我, but not in formal, news-style, or older-person lines. Keep ng- and gw-/kw- for educated or older speech.
pronunciation.example: 你 nei5 → lei5; 我 ngo5 → o5; 國 gwok3 → gok3

pronunciation.rule: Hong Kong Cantonese has six contrastive tones on open or nasal syllables plus three short tones on syllables ending in p, t, k. Guangzhou has seven (it keeps high falling and high level apart).
pronunciation.actor_tip: Use the Jyutping number on every syllable as the pitch target: 1 high level, 2 mid rising, 3 mid level, 4 low falling, 5 low rising, 6 low level.
pronunciation.example: 詩 si1, 史 si2, 試 si3, 時 si4, 市 si5, 是 si6

pronunciation.rule: 唔 is a syllabic nasal m4 (no vowel). 好 hou2, 係 hai6 etc. each take one tone. Minimal pairs: gam3 咁 'so' vs gam2 噉 'in that way'.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Hum the 'm' for 唔 with closed lips for a beat, low-falling. Do not say 'um' or 'wu'.
pronunciation.example: 唔 m4; 咁 gam3 vs 噉 gam2

pronunciation.rule: Jyutping letters with unusual values: z = unaspirated ts, c = aspirated ts, j = English y, oe = rounded 'eu/œ' as in French deux, eo = rounded short 'ö/ɵ', yu = French u.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Do not read z as English z, or j as English j: 嘢 je5 starts with y.
pronunciation.example: 嘢 je5 (y-); 書 syu1; 咗 zo2 (ts-)

pronunciation.rule: Sentence-final particles change meaning by tone: aa3 / aa4 / aa5 / aa6 maa5; lo1 / lo3 / lo4; wo3 / wo5 / wo4; gaa3 / gaa4 / gaa2; ge3 / ge2.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Always speak the particle with the Jyutping number. A wrong tone changes the attitude: 囉 lo1 = 'of course', lo3 = 'let's / okay', lo4 = firm.
pronunciation.example: 係囉 hai6 lo1 vs 走囉 zau2 lo3

pronunciation.rule: Some speakers drop the ng- in a few words: 啱 can be aam1 or ngaam1 (words.hk).
pronunciation.actor_tip: Do not think of 'ng' loss as a mistake. For a young character 啱 sounds like aam1.

tones_intonation.rule: A question can be formed by raising the pitch at the end of a statement, without a question particle. (English Wikipedia)
Hong Kong six tones, by shape: 1 high level (or high falling), 2 mid rising, 3 mid level, 4 low falling, 5 low rising, 6 low level; the three short tones end in -p, -t, -k and sound clipped.
Same particle, different attitude by tone: 呀 aa3 softener; aa4 echo question; aa5 'oh so...?'; lo1 obvious; lo3 'let's go'; lo4 firm. words.hk gives these as separate entries with separate examples.
啦 laa1 stretched out (好啦⋯⋯) signals hesitant agreement; 呀 aa3 stretched out (你呀，同我做晒啲嘢呀～) signals irritation. (words.hk)
唔該 said in an irritated tone means 'shut up / stop it' (words.hk), so the same word can be polite or rude depending on tone and context.

sub_regions.features: Six tones (high level and high falling merged into tone 1). 'Lazy sounds' n→l, ng→zero, gw→g, kw→k are spreading among younger speakers. Uses 的士 (colloquial 老的) for taxi, 巴士 for bus, 七仔 for 7-Eleven. Written Cantonese in Traditional characters.

Seven contrastive tones: high falling and high level are still distinct, although the high-falling tone is said to be disappearing (English Wikipedia). Vocabulary differences for everyday words were not verified in an opened source.
Written Cantonese uses non-standard characters to record speech (佢, 嘅, 唔, 咗, 喺, 冇, 嚟, 啲). The choice between 來 and 嚟 is disputed in the source; this file uses 嚟 for speech.

common_mistakes: Putting 嘅, 咗, 唔, 佢, 喺 into every line. Use them in dialogue, not in narration or formal speech.
Mixing Mandarin words (他們, 在, 不, 沒有, 什麼) with Cantonese particles in one line.
Using one particle for every emotion. Tone matters: 囉 lo1 / lo3 / lo4 and 呀 aa3 / aa4 / aa5 differ in meaning.
Using 咩 or 吓 as a neutral question marker. They signal doubt or surprise.
Using 嘢, 衰嘢, 死嘢, 抵死, 師奶 without noticing their insulting or euphemistic senses.
Reading Jyutping letters as English: z, c, j, oe, eo, yu.
Using lazy sounds (lei5, o5) in formal or older-character lines.
Using Mandarin-style 咗 as a past-tense marker everywhere: 過 marks experience, 緊 marks progress, 咗 marks completion.
generational_notes: Younger Hong Kong speakers show lazy sounds (n→l, ng→zero, gw→g, kw→k), per English Wikipedia; older or educated speakers keep the original distinctions.
Younger speakers use more English loans, abbreviations and puns, per the Hong Kong Cantonese article (source 4 from round 1).
The 5G pun for 唔知 mentioned in round 1 is written play, not a spoken form.
conversion_guidelines: Write in Hong Kong written-Cantonese Traditional characters with Jyutping beneath each line, so the actor can check tones.
In dialogue convert: 他/她→佢, 他们→佢哋, 的→嘅, 不→唔, 没有→冇, 了→咗, 在→喺, 和→同, 什么→乜嘢/咩, 为什么→點解, 谁→邊個, 哪里→邊度, 来→嚟, 一些→啲, 喜欢→鍾意, 知道→知 / 唔知, 累→攰, 家→屋企.
Use the tone-coded particles by emotion: 啦 (suggestion or decision), 囉 (obvious or resigned), 喎 (newly noticed), 㗎 (emphasis), 啩 (guess), 咋 (only), 咩 (doubtful surprise).
Use 唔該 for services, 'excuse me', 'please', and small favours, and 多謝 for gifts and big kindnesses.
Keep narration in standard written Chinese or label it as formal. Keep English loans to about one per scene.
Apply lazy sounds only in casual lines of a young character, and note them for native review.
Insults and edgy words (抵死, 衰嘢, 死嘢, 師奶) must be marked for director approval.

open_questions: Written 嚟 vs 來 and 噉 vs 咁: choose a house style with a Hong Kong native or a dictionary guideline.
喇 laa3 and 嘞 laak3: examples exist, but no opened source states their function range precisely.
Jyutping of 的士 (dik1 si2) was not checked on words.hk.
Hong Kong vs Guangzhou vocabulary differences were not verified apart from tone count and 的士.
The generalization that second syllables of two-syllable loanwords rise (round 1 claim from one article) was removed because it was not verifiable.
Ask a Hong Kong native to review the constructed lines: 冇事嘅，唔使驚。 / 我好攰。 / 我唔知。 / 你食咗飯未呀？
confidence_note: medium-to-high for grammar, particles and Jyutping (dictionary-backed); medium for sub-region and style claims
